knowledge:
- key_parameters:
    - X: Gene expression data matrix with genes as rows and perturbations/samples as columns.
    - restK: Vector indicating the maximum number of non-zero connections for each gene in A. High values increase computation time; 20% to 30% of the number of genes is recommended.
    - topD: Number of branches kept in each level of the grid algorithm tree. 20% to 30% of the number of genes is recommended.
    - topK: Number of potential target genes in each perturbation, used to pre-estimate the perturbation matrix P. 10% to 20% of the number of genes is recommended.
    - P.known: Known perturbation matrix with the same dimensions as X (optional).
    - cFlag: Regression method to use: "geo" (geometric mean / error-in-variable), "sse" (ordinary linear regression), or "ml" (maximum likelihood).
    - pred.net: Prior gene association network matrix (optional).
    - sup.drop: Pattern for using prior network information: 1 for forward pattern, -1 for backward pattern (referred to as sub.drop in some text descriptions).
    - numP: Maximum number of times a gene can be directly targeted by perturbations across all experiments. Suggested to be 25% of the number of genes.
    - noiseLevel: Noise level in each perturbed experiment (only used in "ml" method).
    - cMM.corrected: Flag used in single-row estimation functions; must be set to 1 to specify a prior network (pred.net).
- alternatives: The documentation mentions other ODE-based gene-network reconstruction methods (Gardner et al. and Nelander et al.), but NTW is preferred when the transcriptional perturbation matrix P is unknown, as NTW can estimate both A and P simultaneously.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have steady-state gene expression profiles (from RT-PCR, microarrays, RNA-seq, etc.) from perturbation experiments and want to reconstruct the gene-gene interaction network and/or identify the direct targets of the perturbations.
- pitfalls:
    - Setting high values for restK leads to significantly longer running times.
    - If no prior network is provided (pred.net = NULL), the backward method is used as default (assuming a full prior network).
    - The prior network matrix (pred.net) can only be specified in single-row estimation functions if cMM.corrected is set to 1.

workflows.name: network_and_perturbation_prediction
workflows.intent: Estimate the entire gene interaction network (A) and the perturbation targets matrix (P) from gene expression data, with or without prior network knowledge.
input: gene_expression.csv (matrix of gene expression values with genes as rows and perturbations as columns)
prior_network.csv (optional matrix of prior gene-gene interactions)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the gene expression data and convert to a matrix ;; 2. Set algorithm parameters (restK, topD, topK, numP) ;; 3. Define or generate a prior network matrix (optional) ;; 4. Run the main NTW function to estimate the interaction network and perturbation targets.
workflows.code:
library(NTW)
library(mvtnorm)
data(sos.data)
X<-sos.data
X<-as.matrix(X)
restK=rep(ncol(X)-1, nrow(X))
topD = round(0.6*nrow(X))
topK = round(0.5*nrow(X))
numP = round(0.25*nrow(X))
pred.net<-matrix(round(runif(nrow(X)*nrow(X), min=0, max=1)), nrow(X), nrow(X))
result<-NTW(X, restK, topD, topK, P.known=NULL, cFlag="sse", pred.net = NULL, sup.drop = -1,numP, noiseLevel=0.1)
result<-NTW(X, restK, topD, topK, P.known=NULL, cFlag="sse", pred.net =pred.net, sup.drop = 1,numP, noiseLevel=0.1)

workflows.name: single_row_prediction_unknown_p
workflows.intent: Estimate a single row of the gene interaction matrix (A) and the perturbation targets matrix (P) when the perturbation matrix is unknown (useful for parallelizing computations across genes).
input: gene_expression.csv (matrix of gene expression values with genes as rows and perturbations as columns)
prior_network.csv (optional matrix of prior gene-gene interactions)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the gene expression data and convert to a matrix ;; 2. Set algorithm parameters (restK, topD, topK, numP) ;; 3. Pre-estimate the perturbation matrix using P.preestimation ;; 4. Estimate a single row of A and P using AP.estimation.Srow.
workflows.code:
library(NTW)
library(mvtnorm)
data(sos.data)
X<-sos.data
X<-as.matrix(X)
restK=rep(ncol(X)-1, nrow(X))
topD = round(0.6*nrow(X))
topK = round(0.5*nrow(X))
numP = round(0.25*nrow(X))
pred.net<-matrix(round(runif(nrow(X)*nrow(X), min=0, max=1)), nrow(X), nrow(X))
IX<-P.preestimation(X, topK= round(2*nrow(X)))
result.Srow<-AP.estimation.Srow(r=1,cMM.corrected = 1, pred.net,X, IX,topD, restK, cFlag="sse",sup.drop = -1, numP, noiseLevel=0.1)

workflows.name: single_row_prediction_known_p
workflows.intent: Estimate a single row of the gene interaction matrix (A) when the perturbation matrix (P) is already known.
input: gene_expression.csv (matrix of gene expression values with genes as rows and perturbations as columns)
prior_network.csv (optional matrix of prior gene-gene interactions)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the gene expression data and convert to a matrix ;; 2. Set algorithm parameters (restK, topD, topK) ;; 3. Load or define the known perturbation matrix P.known ;; 4. Estimate a single row of A using A.estimation.Srow.
workflows.code:
library(NTW)
library(mvtnorm)
data(sos.data)
X<-sos.data
X<-as.matrix(X)
restK=rep(ncol(X)-1, nrow(X))
topD = round(0.6*nrow(X))
pred.net<-matrix(round(runif(nrow(X)*nrow(X), min=0, max=1)), nrow(X), nrow(X))
P.known<-matrix(round(runif(nrow(X)*ncol(X), min=0, max=1)), nrow(X), ncol(X))
result.Srow<-A.estimation.Srow(r=1,cMM.corrected = 1, pred.net, X, P.known, topD, restK, cFlag="ml",sup.drop = -1, noiseLevel=0.1)
